issues.description: Deprecation message omits the target removal version that the docstring directive states.
issues.detail: The runtime warning string mentions removal in Falcon 5.0, which matches the TODO and news fragment. Consider also citing the deprecated-since version (4.3) in the warning text for symmetry with the Sphinx directive; minor literate-comment concern, not a correctness issue.

In the new deprecated directive the text reads 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`'. A careful reader will stumble. Knuth-style: code-as-literature means the prose should be as clean as the code.

issues.description: Test asserts warning but does not assert stderr redirect still works.
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected exercises only the stdout path. Since the deprecated function still ships and must remain correct until 5.0, a symmetric assertion on stderr=output would round out the audit. Small literate-test hygiene item; the existing test is sufficient for the deprecation contract.

review.summary: RIGOROUS for what it is: a pure deprecation wrapper around an existing context manager, with no algorithmic surface to audit. Complexity is unchanged (O(1) setup/teardown of sys.stdout/sys.stderr handles), data structures are stdlib TextIO, and the substitution to contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr in tests is mechanically faithful. The only findings are literate-programming nits: a 'stlib' typo, an asymmetric stderr test, and a missing 'deprecated-since' version in the runtime warning text. No correctness, invariant, or performance concerns.
